object_description: large plinth floor carrying three polygonal volumes of different heights
design_condition: a large plinth makes extensive use of the planning perimeter and incorporates the existing green pockets along the street, with three volumes of different heights placed on top

positive: The division into three structures of different heights creates differentiated volumes in keeping with the scale of the neighbourhood
The existing structure of green pockets is incorporated out of consideration for the existing trees and structures the plinth area
Sensibly designed pathways lead to the hall entrance from the inner courtyard
The hall is accentuated by the closed street facade and has a recognisable address
The routing on the site with clear separation of hall, apartment and commercial entrances is functional
The cross-connection in the base area creates cross-references and forecourts
The pentagonal hall is convincing in terms of form, functionality and visitor access
A large shop window in the plinth provides a view of the auditorium
Adjustable ceiling elements regulate the zenithal light and support variable use of the hall
The construction is subtle and beautifully designed and allows exciting changes through the interplay of shapes and light
The commercial space is well positioned and can be used in a variety of ways
The apartments are well oriented and in an attractive central location
The project impresses with a very attractive hall proposal
negative: The large plinth is out of scale with the neighbourhood
The external cubic appearance with the unrecognisable shape of the hall inside is not entirely convincing
The routing is functional but not necessarily atmospheric
The quality and significance of the public square at the street junction are not comprehensible
The cross-reference may be impaired by the tunnel effect of the passageway
Wheelchair access along the east facade does not function as shown, as an existing staircase narrows the space
The kitchen is relatively far from the hall and the service route intersects with that of the toilet users
Only about half of the side storage space can be used as an auditorium extension
Second floor apartments are only conceivable with a well-designed greened flat roof, and the view of the hall volume makes them less attractive
The stair access next to the hall is not correct and reduces the size of the east apartment
The overlapping use of hall and apartments is likely to make it difficult to find a developer
The area and volume of the base appear too massive for the location
The design and possible uses of the outdoor spaces could be improved
